html:
The Mongol and Oirat Code, the "Great Code of the Forty and the Four", was a law code agreed in 1640 at a meeting of Khalkha Mongol and Oirat princes in the Tarbagatai region of Dzungaria. The forty were the Eastern Mongols and the four the Four Oirats, the Western Mongols, who had long fought each other.

The princes, among them the Dzungar ruler Erdeni Batur, wanted peace among themselves at a time when the Manchus, soon the Qing, were rising in the east. The code:

  • set rules for war and mutual defence
  • fixed fines for crimes, mostly paid in livestock
  • regulated hunting, hospitality and marriage
  • made the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism the shared faith, protected lamas and outlawed shamanist images

The Oirat monk Zaya Pandita, who took part, created the Clear Script for the Oirat language in 1648. The code stayed in use among the Oirats of Dzungaria and the Kalmyks on the Volga into the 1700s. It shows how far the Mongols had rebuilt their world around Buddhism since Altan Khan, and Erdeni Batur's Dzungar Khanate became its strongest power.
